title: Who was the best female lead from the Mission Impossible movies (and the worst)?

Emmanuelle Beart might have been underwritten but I did enjoy her spying scenes, which were subtle but spry, and  Michelle Monaghan started out as a generic girlfriend to someone fighting for her survival in a powerful way in MIII. Paula Patton had that cool fight scene where she beats up Lea Seydoux and actually had a strong arc of her own.

title: Halo effect, Nolan and Oppenheimer
text:
Peaking early in one's career can be a challenge for a director. Christopher Nolan is a prime example of this phenomenon, having produced an array of masterpieces early on that set the bar exceedingly high for both himself and others. Movies like "The Prestige," the Batman trilogy, and "Inception" built an unparalleled aura around Nolan, contributing to what is known as the halo effect. However, some of his later movies have been commendable, but they struggled to reach the high standards he had established for himself. 
Take, for instance, today released "Oppenheimer," a good movie without a doubt, but it doesn't quite achieve the same level of excellence as Nolan's earlier works. The halo effect surrounding the director can sometimes deceive us into perceiving any new release as an instant masterpiece.

title: After the success of Oppenheimer...what's next for Nolan?

title: In my opinion, Christopher Nolan is in a slump.
text:
Let me start by saying this is based on my opinion and movie preferences, obviously some people will vehemently disagree.

But after seeing Oppenheimer, I gotta say that Nolan is in a slump.   I'm not saying Nolan is having an M Night Shyamalan fall from grace, but I have been disappointed in his last 3 movies.

Like many others, Christopher Nolan became my favorite director by the movies he put out earlier in his career.  He made movies that really made you think, often required in depth analysis and Youtube video breakdowns to explain all the different things going on.  I absolutely love those type of movies and loved doing all the research/discussions/theories that came from his movies.

I absolutely love Memento (2000) ,The Prestige (2006), Inception (2010), and Interstellar(2014).  Those are my favorites of his.

Batman Beings (2005) and The Dark Knight (2008) are also very entertaining.

But in the past decade, he's released (in my opinion) 3 duds.  

- Dunkirk (2017) was "ok".  There's been much better war movies made, and I thought it was average at best.  I saw it once and don't really have a desire to watch it again.  


- Tenet (2020) I was extremely excited about since it goes back to his roots of crazy sci-fi/time stuff.  However, I was pretty disappointed with it.  While the concept was unique and some of the effects were cool, the story became overly convoluted, the dialogue was inaudible a lot of the time, and the last 30 minute battle scene was an absolute mess.  I have watched this movie a second time, but my opinion didn't change much.


- Oppenheimer (2023):  I went in not expecting this to be a stereotypical Nolan movie, but I was hoping for more than 95% of the movie being people just talking to each other.  There were so many characters introduced, and I felt no connection to any of them, besides Oppenheimer I guess.  I thought the acting and score was good, but besides that it felt like watching a bunch of random clips spliced together. 


So that's 3 movies in the past (*almost*) 10 years that I watched once and never really care to see again.  And if you add in The Dark Knight Rises (2012), which I thought was below-average, I've only enjoyed one of his movies since Interstellar.

Here's my high-level personal breakdown of his movies and whether I enjoyed them or not.
